text.title: Java Spring Boot Enterprise Patterns Worked Examples
text.summary: Worked configuration-binding refactor: eight scattered @Value fields collapsed into one validated @ConfigurationProperties record, with profile-wired beans and a ProblemDetail handler replacing the leaking 500.

section.title: Worked example — the mailer module refactor

example.note: Context: brownfield Boot 3.4 service. `MailService` holds eight `@Value` fields (host, port, user, password, from, maxRetries, timeoutMs, tlsEnabled), and `MailException` currently returns a 500 carrying a stack trace.
Step 1 — inventory every `@Value` and `System.getenv` call and group them by concern. Here they collapse to one concern, `app.mail`, so the plan is a single `MailProperties` record.
Step 3 — map the domain exception to RFC 7807 in the single advice, per `problemdetail-advice`.
Step 4 — replace the `if (env.equals("prod"))` branch with `@Profile("prod") MailSender realSender()` and `@Profile("!prod") MailSender logSender()`, per `config-conditional-on-property`.
Step 5 — boot each profile YAML in turn. A missing `app.mail.host` now fails startup with a `ConstraintViolation` naming the property, instead of surfacing on the first send.
Result: `MailService` injects one dependency instead of eight; a mail-vendor rejection returns a 502 `ProblemDetail` with no stack trace; non-production logs mail instead of sending it.
